blocks.title: One page, every question
blocks.body: Every 'Ask yourself' list and the vendor-questions list from across this course, collected in one place. Use it as a quick reference, a print-out for a workshop, or a starting point for your own team's checklist. Each section links back to the page it came from, where the full context sits.

blocks.title: Before you build (Business Understanding)
blocks.body:
• Is AI actually the right approach here - or would a simpler rule, process or human judgement work with less risk?
  • If AI is appropriate, should this particular system, as currently designed, be built?
  • Have we articulated who benefits from this system, and how significantly - not just who could be harmed?
  • Have we identified who could be harmed by this system?
  • Have we defined success in a way that includes fairness, not just accuracy?
  • Have we engaged the people who will be affected by this system?

blocks.title: Know your data (Data Acquisition and Understanding)
blocks.body:
• Do you know where your training data came from?
  • Was it collected on a lawful basis that covers its use in AI training?
  • Is your dataset representative of the people your AI will affect?
  • Have you checked for known sources of bias?
  • Do you know who prepared or labelled this data, and under what conditions?
  • If someone withdraws consent, can they be removed not just from the dataset but from any model already trained on it - and if not, do the people affected know that?

blocks.title: Explainability (Modeling)
blocks.body:
• Could you explain to someone why your AI made the decision it did about them?
  • Are there groups for whom the AI's reasoning is less well understood?
  • What would you do if an AI decision appeared wrong or unfair?

blocks.title: Before you rely on Copilot's output (Using Copilot Responsibly)
blocks.body:
• Have I checked this output before sending, publishing or acting on it - especially any facts, figures or citations?
  • Would I be comfortable if a colleague knew this came from Copilot rather than me?
  • Am I putting information into a prompt that I wouldn't otherwise be allowed to share - even though Copilot only shows results to people who could already see the source data?
  • If this is an agent or add-on rather than Copilot itself, do I know what it does with the information I give it?
  • If Copilot surfaced something I didn't expect to have access to, do I know who to tell?

blocks.title: Questions to ask an AI vendor (Operationalising Responsible AI)
blocks.body:
These belong in the procurement process itself, not as an afterthought once a contract's signed:

  • What data was this trained on, and has it been tested for bias - can we see the results, not just a statement that testing happened?
  • Is there a model card or equivalent documentation of intended use, known limitations and performance across different groups?
  • Is our data used to train your models? Can we opt out, and is that opt-out retroactive?
  • Have you adopted a recognised framework - ISO/IEC 42001, NIST's AI RMF - or do you have an internal ethics review process?
  • What's the environmental footprint of the model you're asking us to run - can you share compute or energy figures, not just a sustainability statement?
  • What explainability support or audit access do you provide if we need to understand a specific decision?
  • What happens when something goes wrong - what's your incident response commitment, and how would we find out?
